5º de Primaria · Inglés · Tema 2

Past simple: regular verbs

Nombre: ______________________   Fecha: ___________

Qué vas a aprender

  • Talk about finished actions with regular verbs (acciones terminadas)
  • Write the -ed ending with the correct spelling
  • Pronounce -ed in three ways: /t/, /d/ and /ɪd/
  • Make negatives and questions with didn't and did
  • Learn useful regular verbs for everyday life
  • Answer with short answers and ask Wh- questions with did
  • Tell a story in the past and tell the past from the present

Para pensar

Hoy I play al fútbol. Ayer… ¿cómo se dice «jugué»?

Explicación

1. Finished actions

We use the past simple to talk about actions that started and finished in the past: «Yesterday I cleaned my room», «Last Saturday we visited the zoo», «In 2023 my family moved to Valencia».

The action is over: it is not happening now. That's why we usually say when it happened: yesterday, last night, last week, three days ago, in 2022. En castellano: equivale a «limpié», «visitamos», «se mudó». Y una gran ventaja: el verbo inglés no cambia con la persona: I walked, you walked, he walked, we walked.

2. The rule: add -ed

Most verbs are regular. To make the past, we just add -ed: walk → walked, play → played, watch → watched, help → helped, cook → cooked, start → started, open → opened, jump → jumped.

It's the same for all persons: «I listened», «She listened», «They listened». We don't add -s for he or she in the past. Compare: «She plays the piano every day» (present) and «She played the piano yesterday» (past).

3. Spelling: -d, -ied and double letters

Some verbs need a little change. 1. Verbs ending in -e add only -d: like → liked, dance → danced, live → lived, arrive → arrived.

2. Consonant + y changes to -ied: study → studied, carry → carried, try → tried. But vowel + y just adds -ed: play → played, enjoy → enjoyed. 3. Short verbs ending in consonant + vowel + consonant double the last letter: stop → stopped, plan → planned, hug → hugged, drop → dropped.

4. Regular verbs for every day

Most English verbs are regular. Here are some very useful ones, grouped by topic. Learn them in groups: it is easier!

  • At home: clean → cleaned, cook → cooked, wash → washed, tidy → tidied, help → helped, open → opened, close → closed.
  • At school: learn → learned, listen → listened, answer → answered, study → studied, finish → finished, start → started.
  • Free time: play → played, watch → watched, dance → danced, paint → painted, visit → visited, travel → travelled, enjoy → enjoyed.
  • Moving: walk → walked, jump → jumped, climb → climbed, arrive → arrived, stop → stopped, hurry → hurried.
  • Talking: ask → asked, talk → talked, shout → shouted, laugh → laughed, call → called.

Notice that travel doubles the l in British English (travelled), but not in American English (traveled). Both are correct.

Tip: make flashcards with the verb on one side and the past on the other, and a drawing. Review them for five minutes every day.

Another good idea is to keep a verb diary: every evening, write three sentences about your day using regular verbs. «Today I helped my grandma. I played basketball. I listened to music.» After a month, you will know dozens of verbs, and you will use them without thinking. You can also play «Verb tennis» with a friend: one says a verb in the present and the other answers quickly with the past.

5. Three ways to say -ed

The ending -ed doesn't always sound the same. It has three sounds. /t/ after sounds like p, k, s, sh, ch, f: walked («uokt»), jumped, washed, laughed. /d/ after most other sounds: played («pleid»), opened, cleaned, lived.

/ɪd/ only after t or d, and then it adds a new syllable: wanted («uón-tid»), started, needed, decided. En castellano: el error más típico es pronunciar «-ed» entero siempre: «uók-ed». Solo se dice así cuando el verbo acaba en t o d.

6. Negatives with didn't

For the negative we use didn't (did not) + the verb without -ed. «I didn't watch TV.» «He didn't play in the match.» «We didn't finish the puzzle.»

Why without -ed? Because did already tells us it's the past, so the verb goes back to its basic form. Never say «I didn't watched». En castellano: es como en el presente con don't y doesn't: el auxiliar se lleva el tiempo y el verbo queda «limpio».

7. Questions with did

For questions, put Did at the start + subject + verb without -ed: «Did you enjoy the party?» «Did she call you?» Short answers: «Yes, I did.» «No, she didn't.»

With question words: «What did you cook?» «Where did they travel?» «When did the film start?» Ojo: no confundas con was/were: para el verbo to be no usamos did («Were you tired?»), pero para el resto de verbos, sí («Did you walk?»).

8. Short answers and Wh- questions

When someone asks a yes/no question with did, we don't usually answer just «yes» or «no». We use a short answer with did or didn't:

  • «Did you play football yesterday?» – «Yes, I did.» / «No, I didn't.»
  • «Did she clean her room?» – «Yes, she did.» / «No, she didn't.»
  • «Did they watch the film?» – «Yes, they did.»

Never repeat the main verb in a short answer: say «Yes, I did», not «Yes, I played».

To ask for more information, put a question word at the start: Wh- word + did + subject + base form.

  • «What did you watch?» – «I watched a cartoon.»
  • «Where did you play?» – «We played in the park.»
  • «When did they arrive?» – «They arrived at six.»
  • «Who did you visit?» – «I visited my aunt.»
  • «Why did you shout?» – «Because I was angry.»

Remember: after did, the verb is always in the base form, without -ed: «What did you watch?», not «What did you watched?».

9. Sequencing words

When we tell a story in the past, we use sequencing words to put the actions in order: First (primero), Then (luego), Next (después), After that (después de eso) and Finally (por último).

«First, I washed my face. Then, I brushed my teeth. After that, I prepared my bag. Finally, I walked to school.» These words make your text clear and easy to follow. Use a comma after them when they start the sentence.

10. Time expressions: when did it happen?

The past simple goes with time expressions that tell us when something happened. They usually go at the end or at the beginning of the sentence:

  • yesterday (ayer), yesterday morning / afternoon / evening.
  • last + time: last night, last week, last summer, last year, last Monday. Don't use «the»: say «last week», not «the last week».
  • time + ago (hace): two days ago, a week ago, ten years ago. «Ago» always goes after the time.
  • in + year or month: in 2020, in July.
  • on + day or date: on Saturday, on 4th October.
  • at + time: at seven o'clock, at night.
  • when I was + age: when I was five.

Compare: «I visited my cousins last summer.» «Three days ago, we painted the kitchen.» «My parents married in 2010.»

If you start a sentence with a time expression, you can put a comma after it: «Last night, I watched a film.»

11. Reading: a rainy Saturday

Read Nora's text: «Last Saturday it rained all day, so I stayed at home. First, I helped my dad in the kitchen. We baked a carrot cake and it smelled great! Then, I tidied my room and I discovered an old board game under the bed. After that, my brother and I played it for two hours. He laughed a lot because I lost every time. In the evening we watched a film and we chatted with my cousins on the computer. I didn't open my books, but I enjoyed the day.»

Find ten regular verbs. Which ones have /ɪd/? Which verb is in the negative?

12. Let's practise: what did you do?

Play «Find someone who…». Walk around the class and ask: «Did you watch a film last weekend?» «Did you visit your grandparents?» «Did you cook something?» When someone says «Yes, I did», write their name.

Then write a short report: «Lola watched a film. Max visited his grandparents. Nobody cooked.» Repaso: + -ed en afirmativa; didn't + verbo sin -ed en negativa; Did…? + verbo sin -ed en pregunta.

13. Past or present?

It's very important to know when to use the present simple and when to use the past simple.

  • We use the present simple for habits and routines, things that happen usually: «I play tennis every Saturday.» «She walks to school.» Signal words: every day, usually, always, often, on Mondays.
  • We use the past simple for actions that finished in the past: «I played tennis last Saturday.» «She walked to school yesterday.» Signal words: yesterday, last…, …ago, in 2019.

Look at the differences in negatives and questions:

  • Present: «I don't play», «She doesn't play», «Do you play?», «Does she play?».
  • Past: «I didn't play», «She didn't play», «Did you play?», «Did she play?». In the past, did is the same for all persons!

Also, in the present we add -s with he, she, it (she plays), but in the past the form is the same for everybody: I played, she played, they played.

Before you write, look for the time words. They tell you which tense you need.

14. Telling a story: a story map

The past simple is the tense of stories. Before you write one, draw a story map to plan it:

  1. Characters: who is in the story? «A girl called Julia and her dog Bobby.»
  2. Setting: where and when? «In a house, on a Saturday morning.»
  3. Beginning: what happened first? «Mum baked a cake.»
  4. Problem: what went wrong? «The cake disappeared!»
  5. Events: what did the characters do? «Julia searched the kitchen and followed the chocolate spots.»
  6. Ending: how did it finish? «They discovered Bobby and laughed.»

When you write, use sequencing words (first, then, next, after that, finally) and time expressions (one day, last summer, an hour later). Add feelings with was and were: «Mum was angry. The children were surprised.»

Finally, check every verb: did you add -ed? Did you spell it correctly (stopped, studied, danced)? Read your story aloud to a partner and ask: «Did you like it?»

Regular verbs

Ejercicios

  1. Write the past: clean, love, carry, plan.

  2. Complete: «Yesterday we ___ (visit) the castle.»

  3. Complete: «My cat ___ (jump) on the table.»

  4. Make it negative: «I studied for the test.»

  5. Make a question: «You listened to the radio.»

  6. Answer: «Did your team play well?» (yes)

  7. Classify by sound /t/, /d/, /ɪd/: needed, washed, opened.

  8. Correct: «We stoped at the shop and walkt home.»

  9. Order: «didn't / he / the / tidy / room»

  10. Write four sentences about yesterday with First, Then, After that, Finally.

  11. Write the past: clean, study, stop, dance, travel.

  12. Short answer: «Did you watch TV yesterday?» (yes)

  13. Complete with last or ago: «I visited Rome ___ year. I visited Paris two years ___.»

  14. Write three regular verbs you use at school, in the past.

  15. Present or past? «She ___ (walk) to school every day.»

  16. Make a Wh- question: «They arrived at six.» (When)

  17. Correct: «What did you watched last night?»

  18. Change to the past: «I play tennis every Saturday.» (last Saturday)

  19. Write two things you did yesterday and one thing you didn't do.

  20. Complete with in, on or at: «I arrived ___ Monday ___ seven o'clock ___ 2023.»

  21. Draw a story map and write a story of eight sentences in the past simple.

  22. Write the story of the missing cake from Bobby's point of view.

  23. Interview a partner: five questions with did and Wh- words. Write the answers.

  24. Write a paragraph comparing what you usually do on Sundays and what you did last Sunday.

  25. Find five regular verbs in the reading and classify them by the sound of -ed: /t/, /d/, /id/.

Practica

  1. The past of «watch» is…

    1. A) watcht
    2. B) watchied
    3. C) watched

  2. The past of «like» is…

    1. A) liked
    2. B) likeed
    3. C) likied

  3. The past of «study» is…

    1. A) studyed
    2. B) studied
    3. C) studed

  4. The past of «play» is…

    1. A) plaied
    2. B) played
    3. C) playd

  5. The past of «stop» is…

    1. A) stoped
    2. B) stopt
    3. C) stopped

  6. «She didn't ___ the window.»

    1. A) open
    2. B) opened
    3. C) opens

  7. «___ you help your dad?»

    1. A) Do
    2. B) Were
    3. C) Did

  8. In «wanted», -ed sounds…

    1. A) /t/
    2. B) /ɪd/
    3. C) /d/

  9. In «jumped», -ed sounds…

    1. A) /t/
    2. B) /ɪd/
    3. C) /d/

  10. Which word puts actions in order?

    1. A) Then
    2. B) Yesterday
    3. C) Because

  11. «Did you clean your room?» «Yes, I ___.»

    1. A) cleaned
    2. B) did
    3. C) do

  12. «Where ___ you play?»

    1. A) were
    2. B) does
    3. C) did

  13. «I visited Rome three years ___.»

    1. A) last
    2. B) ago
    3. C) before

  14. «She ___ to school every day.»

    1. A) walks
    2. B) walked
    3. C) walk

  15. The past of «travel» in British English is…

    1. A) traveled
    2. B) travelt
    3. C) travelled

Explícalo con tus palabras

Incluye: Para qué sirve el pasado simple; Cómo se forma el pasado de un verbo regular y sus reglas de ortografía; Cómo se pronuncia la terminación -ed; Cómo se hacen negativas y preguntas con did.

Resumen

Glosario

regular verb
Verbo que forma el pasado con -ed.
past simple
Pasado simple.
base form
Forma base del verbo (play).
did
Auxiliar del pasado para preguntas y negativas.
didn't
Did not: negativa en pasado.
short answer
Respuesta corta: Yes, I did.
yesterday
Ayer.
last week
La semana pasada.
ago
Hace (tiempo).
story map
Plano o esquema de una historia.
setting
Lugar y tiempo de una historia.
sequencing words
Palabras para ordenar: first, then, finally.

Tarjetas de repaso

Recórtalas: pregunta delante, respuesta detrás.

Regular verbHace el pasado con -ed.

consonante + y → -iedstudy → studied.

/t/ /d/ /ɪd/walked · played · wanted.

Soluciones

  1. C) Regla general: + -ed.
  2. A) Acaba en -e: + d.
  3. B) Consonante + y → -ied.
  4. B) Vocal + y: + ed.
  5. C) Se dobla la consonante.
  6. A) Tras didn't, sin -ed.
  7. C) Pregunta en pasado: Did.
  8. B) Tras t: sílaba nueva.
  9. A) Tras p: /t/.
  10. A) Then = luego.
  11. B) Short answer with did.
  12. C) Wh- + did + subject.
  13. B) Time + ago.
  14. A) Habit → present.
  15. C) Double l.

Soluciones de los ejercicios

  1. cleaned, loved, carried, planned.
  2. visited.
  3. jumped.
  4. I didn't study for the test.
  5. Did you listen to the radio?
  6. Yes, it did. / Yes, they did.
  7. needed /ɪd/, washed /t/, opened /d/.
  8. We stopped at the shop and walked home.
  9. He didn't tidy the room.
  10. Model answer: First, I walked to school. Then, I played with my friends. After that, I helped my mum. Finally, I watched TV.
  11. cleaned, studied, stopped, danced, travelled.
  12. Yes, I did.
  13. last, ago.
  14. Example: learned, listened, answered.
  15. walks (present simple).
  16. When did they arrive?
  17. What did you watch last night?
  18. I played tennis last Saturday.
  19. Open answer. Example: I cleaned my room. I helped my dad. I didn't watch TV.
  20. on, at, in.
  21. Open answer with sequencing words.
  22. Open answer in the first person: I smelled the cake…
  23. Open answer.
  24. Open answer with present and past simple.
